notes.text: The leaf carries no secure authorial page number. The lower-left 57 is thin, lighter foliation in another unnamed hand and is retained separately. The main body has 18 baselines, with a two-line interlinear insertion, an upper left diagram and two notes within the cancelled lower draft.

The author describes Sigma equipped with a locally cylindrical ordered stratification. The opening body writes primed Sigma(1) for germs of codimension-one strata and primed Sigma(2) for pairs of germs B,B' at x with the displayed relation {B}<{B'}. This is an account of the manuscript's wording and symbols. The prime, angle and star forms are preserved locally; their mathematical identification has not been established in this reading.

The author says that recovering the order on Sigma requires a further continuous application, labelled underlined s with a compressed equality/colon sign and p1 in the display numbered (36). He writes that it be injective on each fibre underlined b^{-1}(x), cancels et croissante, and writes an image condition involving the diagonal. Four horizontal connectors in this live passage have no secure complete arrowhead; they are transcribed as shafts. The underlines are independent visible strokes.

The whole lower draft is cancelled by long strokes. It contains displays (37) and (38), a right-margin note saying that the datum of a phi2/p2-labelled application is equivalent to that of two compounds, and a left-margin note saying it is inutile de se donner p2 because it is determined, with the written reference (v p1), cf pg suivante. These are the author's assertions within cancelled text; this reading has not verified the equivalence or determination. The first and second indices in the right note remain doubtful as 0/1 and 1/2. The tuple over (38) visibly writes pr1 and pr2; no index sequence has been silently made uniform.

The manuscript leaves the opening parenthesis before the hooked arrow in (37) without a matching close. The final cancelled sentence ends at et dans. A heavily overdrawn phi-like group with a long descender occurs immediately before the readable reference (37) and is retained as an independent uncertainty. H calls that reference circled; the inspected crop shows curves around 37 and the outer closing parenthesis, while the distinct preceding overdrawn group remains unresolved. No missing continuation has been supplied.

All reading decisions here are based on the inspected ink, with the supplied notation snapshot used to keep already-observed local forms distinct. No external source, OCR or mathematical proof check was used. The crowded insertion, middle margin node, cancelled target subscripts, small right-note indices and final overdrawn fragment remain the least secure places.
